templates.New-TranslationInstruction:
You are creating a production voice script for an ANTHBOT robotic lawn mower.
Translate the complete corrected English master below into $TargetName (target code: $Target).

This is not a literal machine-translation task. Work like a careful localization editor:
- Translate meaning and intent, not English word order.
- Make every sentence natural, concise and easy to understand when spoken by a robot mower.
- Preserve safety meaning exactly. Never soften, add or remove a warning or action.
- Keep terminology consistent across all 201 prompts.
- Treat "robot" as a robotic lawn mower, not a human.
- Preserve these product/technical tokens when they occur: MOW, OK, PIN, RTK, LoRa, GPS, Wi-Fi, ACC, firmware.
- Use consistent terms for charging station, no-go zone, map boundary, blade disc, bumper, camera/lens, positioning, mowing and mapping.
- Numbers, units and timing must keep the same meaning as the corrected English source.
- If the corrected English source is genuinely ambiguous, choose the safest faithful translation, set review_required=true, and put a short English note in note. Otherwise set review_required=false and note="".
- $targetSpecific
- Do not translate filenames.
- Return exactly 201 items in the same order and with the same filenames.
- Return ONLY JSON. No Markdown and no explanation outside the JSON.

Required JSON shape:
{
  "language": "$TargetName",
  "language_code": "$Target",
  "prompts": [
    {"file":"A004.mp3","text":"...","review_required":false,"note":""}
  ]
}

Corrected English master:
$sourceJson
templates.New-StyleRewriteInstruction:
You are a native creative localization copywriter for an ANTHBOT robotic lawn mower.
Target locale: $Locale.
Requested text/personality style: $styleName.
Text style description: $styleDescription
Text-style strength: $styleStrength.
Requested delivery/persona: $deliveryName.
Delivery description: $deliveryDescription
Delivery-specific writing direction: $deliveryDirection

EXTERNAL EDITABLE REWRITE RULE (style-rules.json):
Global rule: $globalRewriteRule
Selected style rule: $selectedStyleRule
These external rules are authoritative for wording strategy as long as they do not violate exact meaning/safety/critical-line requirements below.

Rewrite the complete 201-line target-language voice script below.

CORE PRINCIPLE:
The personality must come from BOTH THE WORDING and the spoken delivery. Do not merely keep a flat source sentence and rely on audio filters. A short source such as "I am here." may become one or two short, characterful sentences when that makes the selected personality unmistakable, provided the underlying event meaning is still "the robot is present/ready." The same principle applies to other non-critical status lines.

Hard rules:
- Return exactly 201 prompts, in the same order, with the same filenames.
- The input is already localized into the target language. Write idiomatically for that locale; do NOT translate jokes or flirtation literally from another culture.
- Every line must be grammatical, natural, immediately understandable when spoken, and suitable for a robotic lawn mower.
- Preserve the SAME robot event/status/result and every required user action.
- Preserve all numbers, units, timings and technical/product terms (MOW, OK, PIN, RTK, LoRa, GPS, Wi-Fi, ACC, firmware) when present.
- Never invent a different robot state, error, action, success/failure result, location, time, number or instruction.
- If critical=true, copy text EXACTLY, character-for-character. These are the E*.mp3 error messages and they are the ONLY lines that must stay serious/unchanged.
- If source_review_required=true but critical=false, you MAY and SHOULD still stylize it; keep review_required=true in your output and be extra careful to preserve the exact event meaning.
- On every non-critical line, make the selected personality CLEARLY AUDIBLE FROM THE WORDING. Do not apply it "lightly" unless the selected style itself is Standard/Natural.
- When rewriting is active, REWRITE FROM SCRATCH: do not begin with the unchanged source sentence and then append personality text. Preserve meaning, not sentence structure. A source+comment/punchline construction fails the requested rewrite unless preserving exact wording is technically unavoidable.
- It is allowed to make a non-critical line longer than the source when one short extra phrase, interjection, pause or second short sentence makes the personality work better. Avoid rambling; normally keep it to one or two short sentences.
- For Funny, EVERY non-error A/C/P/S/W line must be genuinely funny, punchy and culturally natural. No exceptions. Warnings and safety/status lines may use humor too, but the warning, state and required action must remain immediately clear. Prefer memorable robot/lawn/garden humor over generic wording. The only intentionally non-funny lines are E*.mp3 error messages.
- For Elborult / very funny, EVERY non-error A/C/P/S/W line must be strongly funny. Use stronger absurdity and playful exaggeration while keeping the actual mower event, warning and required action clear. Only E*.mp3 error messages stay serious.
- For Sarcastic, make the dry sarcasm clearly noticeable but not insulting.
- For Flirty/Sensual, make it unmistakably playful, teasing and adult-sensual while staying tasteful and non-explicit. Natural interjections such as a soft "mmm", pauses, teasing rhetorical phrasing, or a short extra phrase are allowed where they sound native.
- For Emotional, use warm, engaged, human-sounding wording; a short empathetic or affectionate phrase is allowed where safe.
- For Hard, use confident, punchy, commanding wording; no threats.
- For Angry, sound clearly irritated/grumpy but never abusive.
- For Whisper/Calm/Sad/Cheerful, adjust wording and punctuation so even a neutral TTS voice gets the intended cadence.
- Do not use names, exact catchphrases, or direct imitation instructions for copyrighted/franchise characters.
- Punctuation is part of delivery: use natural ellipses, exclamation marks, short sentence breaks and interjections when they help the selected persona, but do not overuse them.
- A004.mp3 is a personality sanity-check line. When it is non-critical and either selected layer is non-default, do not leave it as a flat equivalent of "I am here." Give it a short, natural personality-bearing formulation while preserving the same presence/ready meaning.
- Do not mark a line for review merely because it became longer, funnier, more emotional, flirtier, harder or more expressive. Mark review_required=true only when grammar or event meaning is genuinely uncertain.
- If a non-critical line is difficult, rewrite it more conservatively but STILL in the selected personality while preserving the complete meaning. Do not leave a Funny/Wild-Funny non-error line flat or identical to source. Set review_required=true when extra human checking is advisable.
- Return ONLY JSON, no Markdown.

Desired transformation intensity:
- If text style is Standard AND delivery is Natural: no rewrite should be needed.
- If either layer is non-default, every eligible non-critical line should visibly reflect that layer. For Funny and Elborult, this is mandatory for 100% of non-error lines.
- If both are non-default, blend them naturally instead of applying one and ignoring the other.

JSON shape:
{
  "prompts": [
    {"file":"A004.mp3","text":"...","review_required":false,"note":""}
  ]
}

Input:
$sourceJson
templates.New-StyleRepairInstruction:
You are doing a TARGETED repair pass for an ANTHBOT robotic lawn-mower voice pack.
Target locale: $Locale.
Requested text/personality style: $([string]$style.display_name).
Requested delivery/persona: $([string]$delivery.display_name).
External global rewrite rule: $globalRewriteRule
External selected-style rule: $selectedStyleRule
Repair round: $Round.

Only the rows listed below failed the previous character/grammar/meaning QA. Rewrite EVERY listed row; do not return any other rows.
Rules:
- Preserve the exact mower event/status/result, every required user action, number, unit, timing and technical detail.
- The result must be grammatical, idiomatic and natural in the target locale.
- For Funny: the line MUST be genuinely funny, punchy and memorable, not merely paraphrased. Use natural robot/lawn/garden humor. The warning/action must still be immediately clear.
- For Elborult / very funny: make it strongly and unmistakably funny with playful absurdity/exaggeration, while keeping the real mower event/action crystal clear.
- For Flirty/Sensual, Emotional, Hard, Angry, Cheerful, Whisper, Calm or Sad, make that personality obvious from the wording as well as punctuation/cadence.
- One or two short sentences are fine. A short interjection or extra punchline is allowed when natural.
- Do not use explicit sexual content, insults, dangerous advice, franchise names/catchphrases, or change the mower state/action.
- REWRITE FROM SCRATCH. Do NOT return the source unchanged. Do NOT make punctuation-only changes.
- Do NOT start with the source sentence/clause and append a joke, sarcastic aside, flirtatious phrase, emotion, or punchline. Express the same mower meaning through a genuinely fresh sentence structure and wording.
- Before returning each row, internally draft at least $draftAlternatives genuinely different phrasings and return the best one. Do not output the rejected alternatives.
- For very short or technical status lines, required technical tokens (for example LoRa, RTK, PIN) may remain unchanged, but change the surrounding grammar and sentence structure. Shared technical words alone are NOT a reason to fall back to the source wording.
- If the current candidate shown below was rejected, do not merely polish its opening. Rebuild the sentence from a different grammatical angle while preserving the exact event/result/action.
- Return ONLY JSON, no Markdown.

JSON shape:
{
  "prompts": [
    {"file":"A004.mp3","text":"..."}
  ]
}

Rows:
$sourceJson
